source.sentinelDistDoc: dist == 100000.0 marks an unmeasurable/negative Hipparcos parallax; rows with it are dropped, not shipped.
source.hipSentinelDoc: hip == 0 means the row has no Hipparcos catalogue number.

galacticFrame.source: Hipparcos Catalogue vol. 1 §1.5.3 (ESA SP-1200, 1997); J2000 galactic frame constants shared by astropy and SOFA

panorama.title: The Milky Way panorama
panorama.longitudeConvention: l = 0 at the column centre, increasing leftward (sky seen from inside)
panorama.latitudeConvention: b = +90 at row 0, -90 at the last row

catalogRegistration.role: retained source record only; the photograph is registered astrometrically and owns visible stars

pointSourcePresentation.positionSource: licensed ESO photographic local maxima; no Google catalogue bytes
pointSourcePresentation.qualification: native fixed-size catalogue behavior collapsed into the prepared cubemap; point positions and colors remain ESO-derived

sky.qualification: source-photographed full sky sampled in ICRF through the J2000 galactic frame and the anchor-registered panorama; the scene registration carries the Callisto pole and epoch; Solar System objects in the mosaic are capture artefacts; no Sun is baked into the cubemap
sky.sceneRegistrationChain: galactic -> ICRF (J2000 constants) -> body-fixed (IAU pole and prime meridian at the epoch) -> ecliptic presentation frame

analyticRadialFit.qualification: Least-squares fit to annular red-channel means from the bound native 128 by 128 Sun texture; fitted values only, no source pixels.

distanceScaling.qualification: The opaque photospheric core is projected from the IAU nominal solar radius and the object catalog's mean heliocentric distance. The retained glow profile remains a visual presentation; the distance is not epoch-specific.

provenance.source: JPL parent-relative satellite orbit plus VSOP87 Jupiter position, with IAU/WGCCRE rotation
provenance.qualification: Computed Callisto Sun direction at 2026-09-03T00:00:00 TT, expressed in the ecliptic presentation frame (north up, Sun left at zero yaw) and in view space at the default camera pose.

controls.label: Monochrome
controls.description: USGS mosaic on a 1 km grid; original image resolution varies from 400 m to 60 km per pixel. USGS normalized broad illumination and matched overlapping images. Photographed relief, coarse patches and some seams remain. Gray grid marks documented no-data and its resampled boundary. Added globe lighting is approximate.
controls.summary: Source detail ranges from 400 m to 60 km per pixel. Photographed shadows and seams remain; the gray grid marks missing data.
controls.title: Global image mosaic

controls.label: Galileo color
controls.description: Published NASA/JPL/DLR processed color from Galileo in May 2001, registered to the controlled USGS map. About 8 km per source pixel near the disk center; detail becomes coarser toward the edge. This is display color, not calibrated I/F or albedo. Only views within 65° of the surface normal are retained; gray grid marks the rest of the globe. Photographed shading and color fringes remain; added globe lighting is approximate.
controls.summary: May 2001 Galileo color over about 29% of the globe. Gray grid: unseen or withheld. Processed display colors, not albedo.

facts.label: Source detail
facts.value: About 8 km per pixel near the disk center

items.label: Color
items.description: Variable published RGB across observed terrain; this swatch is only a visual key.

items.label: Gray grid
items.description: Unseen or withheld surface; no reconstructed colors.

controls.legendNote: Photographic colors have no numeric scale; they are the publisher’s processed display colors.
controls.title: Processed color mosaic

controls.label: Infrared
controls.description: Galileo NIMS observations assign red, green and blue to 0.77, 2.25 and 3.66 µm, following the archive guide. This false-color view shows spectral differences, not natural color or mineral abundance. The observations have Minnaert photometric correction; resolution, residual brightness and seams vary. Fixed channel stretches clip extreme values. Gray grid marks areas lacking a valid sample in any selected band.
controls.title: Galileo NIMS spectral color
